## Audit Summary: no LLM spend found

I ran `list_call_sites` (0 call sites, 0 files) and then, since the task said 1 source file was in scope, confirmed directly by reading the repo: it contains exactly one file, `app.py` — a 10-line FastAPI app:

```python
from fastapi import FastAPI
app = FastAPI()

@app.get("/items/{item_id}")
def read_item(item_id: int):
    return {"item_id": item_id, "price": item_id * 2.5}

@app.get("/health")
def health():
    return {"ok": True}
```

Two broad `search_code` sweeps confirmed there is nothing to find:
- Provider/SDK patterns (`openai|anthropic|gemini|ChatCompletion|generate_content|messages.create|chat.completions`) → **no matches**.
- General import/client/API-key sweep (`import|require|api_key|sdk|client`) → only `from fastapi import FastAPI` matched.

**Per-axis disposition** (every axis in the checklist ruled out on the same concrete grounds — there is no LLM call site to examine):
- Caching, dedup, redundant/skippable calls, over-retrieval (RAG), batching, oversized/static context, tool-schema bloat, serialization waste, tool-response bloat, tool-output overflow, code-payload bloat, over-generation, conversation-history bloat, retry/error-loop, guardrail/judge overhead, embedding waste, n>1/speculative — **N/A, no LLM call exists to carry any of these costs.**
- model_mismatch, eliminate-the-call, reasoning-token waste, multimodal/image cost, prompt/context compression — **N/A, same reason.**
- Agent-loop-only axes (inner-turn model uniformity, agent-memory re-injection) — **ruled out at the gate**: no agent framework (LangGraph, AgentExecutor, CrewAI, AutoGen, OpenAI Agents SDK, LlamaIndex agents, semantic-kernel) and no hand-rolled while/for loop feeding tool results back into a model call anywhere in the file.

The two endpoints do local, deterministic work only (`item_id * 2.5` arithmetic; a static health dict) — there's no prompt, no provider HTTP call, no token cost of any kind.

I recorded `set_repo_cost(total_monthly_spend_usd=0)` with the evidence above as basis, and emitted **zero findings** — inventing a caching/model-swap/dedup finding here would be exactly the "padded finding to fill the checklist" the audit instructions tell me not to do. ## Audit summary: `moderate.py` (1 call site, 1 file, entire repo)

**Total repo spend: ~$1/mo** (set via `set_repo_cost`) — this is a genuinely tiny codebase: one function, one API call, no callers visible anywhere in the repo. The dollar amounts below are small in absolute terms but the *percentage* waste (94% on the model swap) is real and would scale linearly if this function is actually invoked more than the unmeasured 10,000/mo default assumes.

### Findings shipped
1. **model_mismatch** — `gpt-4o` doing a single-word spam/ham classification that a mini-tier model handles fine. Fix attached (`model="gpt-4o-mini"`), saving ≈$0.82/mo at assumed volume (94% cheaper on the swap). **Caveat: shadow_verify came back INCONCLUSIVE** — this sandbox has no live OpenAI key, so I could not measure real gpt-4o-vs-mini agreement (the tool refuses to fake it). Shipped as an unverified structural edit, not a confirmed-safe swap — re-run shadow_verify with real credentials before trusting it blindly.
2. **over_generation** — no `max_tokens` cap on a call whose correct output is exactly one word. Fix attached (`max_tokens=5`), quality-neutral (gpt-4o isn't a reasoning model, so capping carries no truncation risk), ≈$0.375/mo saved if the model ever drifts into a verbose reply.

### Axes ruled out (with reason)
- **Caching**: system prompt is 9 tokens — far below any provider's cacheable minimum (~1,024 tokens). Nothing to cache.
- **Dedup / batching**: `is_spam()` has zero callers anywhere in the repo (confirmed via `trace_symbol` and a full regex sweep for loops/cron/batch) — no evidence of a loop or repeated-identical-input pattern to dedupe or batch.
- **Over-retrieval / RAG, tool-schema bloat, serialization, tool-response/tool-output bloat, code-payload bloat, conversation-history bloat, retry/error-loop, guardrail/judge overhead, embedding waste, n>1/speculative, multimodal, reasoning-token waste, prompt/context compression**: none apply — this is a single-turn, no-tools, no-history, non-reasoning, text-only call with a 9-token prompt.
- **Eliminate-the-call (regex replacement)**: attempted via `verify_elimination` with a keyword regex — the tool errored (missing `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` in this sandbox), so agreement could not be measured. Not shipped: spam detection is also a poor deterministic-rule fit in general (that's why ML classifiers exist for it), so I didn't force an unverified regex finding.
- **Agent-loop axes (inner-turn model uniformity, agent-memory re-injection)**: no agent framework or hand-rolled loop anywhere in the repo — gated out in one line per the instructions.

**★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────**
Two of my verification tools (`shadow_verify`, `verify_elimination`) came back INCONCLUSIVE/errored here because this sandbox has no live provider API keys — that's a deliberate safety property of the audit tooling ("no proxy or substitute model is used"), not a bug. It's the same discipline good engineering teams should apply to their own LLM-swap PRs: don't merge "should be fine" model downgrades without an actual side-by-side eval on real traffic, even when the swap looks obviously safe.

Question + completion tokens (input+output)

findings.title: POLICY_DOC repeats one sentence 400x — 96% of every call's input tokens carry zero new information
findings.root_cause: Line 4 builds the system prompt as `("All refunds are processed within 14 days subject to review. " * 400)` — the identical sentence duplicated 400 times. Measured: the resulting POLICY_DOC is 3,904 tokens (count_tokens), while the distinct informational content is 16 tokens (count_tokens on the single sentence). Every one of the ~10,000 monthly calls pays for 3,888 tokens of pure verbatim repetition that adds no information the model can use — it's not a real 400-paragraph policy, it's one paragraph glued to itself 400 times. This is the single biggest lever on this repo: it doesn't require caching, model changes, or shadow verification because the semantic content is byte-for-byte identical before and after the fix.
findings.fix: Deduplicate POLICY_DOC to its single distinct sentence. Output is provably unchanged: the model receives the exact same fact, just once instead of 400 times. This alone removes ~99.6% of the system-prompt tokens on every call, and coincidentally makes the caching finding below moot (the trimmed prompt falls under the ~1,024 token minimum where Anthropic prompt caching stops being worth it) — apply this fix first.

findings.title: Static system prompt sent uncached on every call (fallback if POLICY_DOC bloat isn't trimmed)
findings.root_cause: POLICY_DOC (3,904 tokens measured) is a Python module-level constant — byte-identical on every call, never mutated — yet `system=POLICY_DOC` is passed as a plain string with no `cache_control` block, so Anthropic re-reads and re-bills the full 3,904 tokens at full input price on every single request. There is no dynamic content in the prefix (no timestamp/uuid), so nothing blocks caching — it's simply never enabled. NOTE: this finding is computed against the CURRENT untrimmed 3,904-token doc as an alternative fix path; if the oversized_context finding (POLICY_DOC dedup) is applied instead, this saving mostly evaporates because the trimmed 16-token prompt falls below Anthropic's ~1,024-token cache minimum. Apply ONE of the two, not both — the trim is larger, simpler, and zero-risk, so it is the primary recommendation and this is the fallback.
findings.fix: Mark POLICY_DOC as an ephemeral cache block with a 1-hour TTL (requires the `extended-cache-ttl-2025-04-11` beta header). Economics: read_rate=0.1 (Anthropic cache-hit reads cost 10% of input price), write_premium=2.0x (1-hour TTL). Assuming the default 5-min TTL: at 10,000 calls/month spread over 8,640 five-minute windows (~1.16 calls/window), average reuse (1.16) is BELOW the break-even reuse count (~1.28) for the 1.25x 5-min write premium — the default TTL would likely net LOSE money at this volume unless traffic clusters heavily in bursts. The 1-hour TTL is recommended instead: 720 windows/month, ~13.9 calls/window, comfortably above its break-even reuse count of ~2.1.

findings.title: FAQ answer generated by LLM when the entire knowledge base is one static fact — candidate for elimination
findings.root_cause: POLICY_DOC contains exactly ONE distinct fact ("refunds are processed within 14 days subject to review"). The model has no other information to draw on, so regardless of how a customer phrases their question, the only grounded answer it can give is a restatement of that single fact — anything more specific (e.g. "are used items refundable?", "do I get store credit?") the model can only guess at or hedge on, which is a correctness/consistency risk, not just a cost one. This is the LLM-for-deterministic-work pattern (formatting/templating a known answer) rather than genuine open-ended generation. Full elimination is the largest possible lever (100% of this call's cost) but is a QUALITY-AFFECTING change (the exact wording customers see changes) and is a generation task, not a fixed-label classification, so verify_elimination (which judges regex-vs-LLM label agreement) does not apply here — there is no regex to verify. Per audit discipline this stays a prose recommendation, not an apply-ready patch, until a human validates canned-response coverage against the real spread of questions this endpoint receives.
findings.fix: Recommend: replace the LLM call with a templated response (e.g. an f-string acknowledging the question + the fixed policy sentence) for the current single-fact policy doc, OR add a cheap keyword/intent gate that only invokes the LLM for questions outside what the static policy covers (e.g. "refund" not present, or a complaint/escalation) and returns the canned answer otherwise. Ship only after checking real question logs to confirm most traffic really is answerable from the one fact — do not apply blind.

findings.title: claude-sonnet-4 used for a bounded single-fact FAQ restatement — cheaper tier likely sufficient (unverified: frontier unreachable for shadow test)
findings.root_cause: The task at this call site is bounded and simple: restate one fixed policy fact in response to varied phrasings of a refund question, single-turn, no tools, no multi-step reasoning. 03-uncached-faq.summary:
## Audit Summary

`erabot`'s worklist has exactly **1 call site**: `faq.py:8`, a `claude-sonnet-4` call that answers customer refund questions. Total estimated spend: **$132.57/month** — small in absolute terms, but **~88% of it is reclaimable**, and the biggest win costs nothing in output quality.

**Findings emitted (4):**
1. **`oversized_context`** ($116.64/mo, quality-neutral, apply-ready) — `POLICY_DOC` is one sentence glued to itself 400 times (`sentence * 400`). Measured: 3,904 tokens sent vs. 16 tokens of actual distinct content. Trimming to the single sentence is provably output-identical and is the primary fix — apply this first.
2. **`caching`** ($89.39/mo, quality-neutral, apply-ready, *alternative* to #1) — the same static doc, if not trimmed, should at minimum be sent as a 1-hour ephemeral cache block; I showed the default 5-min TTL actually loses money at this call volume (avg 1.16 calls/5-min-window < break-even 1.28), so I shipped the 1-hour TTL variant instead. Explicitly flagged as non-additive with finding #1.
3. **eliminate-the-call** ($132.57/mo ceiling, quality-affecting, prose-only) — since the policy doc holds exactly one fact, the LLM call itself is a candidate for a templated/gated response. Not shipped as a patch (it's a generation task, not a regex-classification `verify_elimination` can check) — flagged for human validation against real question logs.
4. **`model_mismatch`** ($88.38/mo projected, quality-affecting, prose-only) — claude-sonnet-4 for a bounded single-fact restatement is a plausible downgrade candidate, but `shadow_verify` came back **INCONCLUSIVE twice** (the frontier model isn't reachable from this sandbox — no live Anthropic key). Per audit discipline, I reported the finding with its shadow_id and list-price-only numbers rather than hiding or fabricating a verdict.

**Axes swept and ruled out** (all read directly against `faq.py`, the repo's only call site): dedup (no recurring-document pipeline, this is a live per-question endpoint), over-retrieval/RAG (no retrieval step exists), batching (single independent per-request call, no bulk loop), tool-schema bloat (no `tools=` param), serialization waste (no structured JSON/array data in the prompt), tool-response/tool-output bloat (no agent loop, no tool results fed back), code-payload bloat (no source code sent), over-generation (`max_tokens=400` is a reasonable cap for a short answer, not a reasoning model, no evidence of runaway output), conversation-history bloat (single-turn call, no message history accumulation), retry/error-loop waste (no retry logic present), guardrail/judge overhead (no judge/guardrail wrapper), embedding waste (no embeddings used), n>1/speculative generation (single completion, no `n` param), reasoning-token waste (standard model, no extended thinking), multimodal cost (text-only), prompt/context compression (the bloat here is literal verbatim duplication, not dense unique prose — already covered by finding #1's dedup, not a compression-algorithm case). **Agent-loop-only axes** (inner-turn model uniformity, agent-memory re-injection): ruled out in one line — no agent framework, no loop, no multi-step control flow anywhere in this repo; a single function makes a single call.

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
The two biggest wins here targeted the *exact same line of code* from two different angles, and they don't stack: `POLICY_DOC * 400` is both "bloated" (99.6% redundant tokens) and "uncached" (no `cache_control`), but fixing the redundancy makes caching moot — the trimmed 16-token prompt falls below Anthropic's ~1,024-token cache minimum, so there'd be nothing left worth caching. This is exactly why the audit brief insists on separating root causes even when a fix collides: reporting only "add caching" would have banked $89/mo and left $28/mo of avoidable spend on the table forever, since nobody would revisit an already-"fixed" line.

The other lesson is about shadow-testing honesty: when `shadow_verify` couldn't reach `claude-sonnet-4` at all (no live key in this sandbox), the correct move wasn't to guess at a quality delta from memory — it's to report the finding as INCONCLUSIVE with list-price-only numbers and withhold the apply-ready patch. An audit tool that fabricates a verdict when it can't measure one is worse than a shorter report.

findings.title: Uncapped completions + no brevity instruction — every agent turn generates a full verbose reply
findings.root_cause: agent.py:7 calls client.chat.completions.create() with no max_tokens and no system prompt telling the model to be terse on continuation turns. gpt-4o (non-reasoning, so a hard cap is safe) is left to decide length itself; measured, a full-plan-restating reply runs ~313 tokens (count_tokens) vs a terse progress-only update of ~43 tokens for the same underlying progress — a ~7x difference on turns 2-6 of every task, where the model has no instruction to stop re-explaining context it already stated in turn 1.
findings.fix: Add a system message instructing terse, incremental progress updates after turn 1, and cap max_tokens=400 (generous enough for the legitimate turn-1 plan, tight enough to stop runaway restatement). Quality-neutral: turn 1 still gets its full plan; only the redundant re-explaining on later turns is removed.

findings.title: Full conversation history resent every turn with no windowing — unbounded prompt growth
findings.root_cause: agent.py:5-9: `history` only ever grows (each turn appends the assistant reply and the FULL list is resent as `messages=history` on the next call, line 7) — there is no windowing or summarization. Modeled over a 6-turn task with ~313-token replies, cumulative input tokens sent across the task total 5,349 vs 2,219 if only the original task + the single most recent turn were resent (older turns add no new information the model needs to continue past a terse progress update). That's a 3,130 token/task reduction on the priciest-growing part of the prompt.
findings.fix: After each turn, collapse history to [original task, most recent assistant turn] instead of keeping every prior turn — the loop doesn't do tool-result accumulation or multi-fact recall, so older turns are pure resent overhead, not needed context.

findings.title: No max_iterations bound on the agent loop — cost exposure is unbounded per task
findings.root_cause: agent.py:6-11: `while True:` has no turn cap; the only exit is `"TASK_COMPLETE" in out`, a naive substring check on the model's own free-text output. If the model never emits that exact string (forgets it, phrases completion differently, or the task genuinely stalls), the loop keeps calling the API, resending an ever-growing history each time, until it either exhausts the model's context window (raising an exception) or runs indefinitely. Conservatively modeling only a modest tail — 5% of tasks averaging 20 turns instead of the well-behaved 6 — costs $0.217/task vs $0.067/task if capped at 10 turns; the far worse (unquantified) case is a run that grows until it hits the context-window ceiling, which would cost roughly $65+ in a single task before failing.
findings.fix: Bound the loop with `for _ in range(MAX_TURNS)` (e.g. MAX_TURNS=10) and return the best-effort last reply if the cap is hit instead of looping (or crashing on context overflow) unbounded. This repo is a single 11-line agent loop, so the audit's job was to prove that "one tiny call site" can still hide four *independent* cost defects — the taxonomy exists precisely so you don't stop at the first one (over-generation) and miss the compounding ones stacked on top of it (history growth × turn count × model choice).

## Audit results — `agent.py` (1 call site, gpt-4o, entire repo)

**Total estimated spend: ~$414/mo** (all attributable to this one loop — see breakdown in `set_repo_cost`). Four findings emitted, three shipped as apply-ready patches; one (model swap) explicitly held back because it couldn't be verified.

|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | No `max_tokens` / no brevity instruction — every turn re-explains the whole plan (313 tok measured vs 43 tok terse, count_tokens-grounded) | over_generation | $135 | ✅ patch |
| 2 | Full history resent every turn, unbounded growth (5,349 vs 2,219 tok/task windowed) | oversized_context | $78 | ✅ patch |

| 4 | Same gpt-4o hardcoded on every turn, including routine "continue" turns | model_mismatch | $252 (**unverified — theoretical list price only**) | ❌ no patch |

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
Finding #4 is the interesting one: `shadow_verify(gpt-4o → gpt-4o-mini)` came back **INCONCLUSIVE**, not SAFE or UNSAFE — this sandbox has no live OpenAI key, so the tool correctly refused to fake a quality comparison rather than silently substituting a stand-in model. That's the system doing its job: an unreachable candidate gets dropped, not faked, and per the audit rules an unverified model swap stays a prose recommendation, never an apply-ready patch. The $252/mo figure is real *list-price* arithmetic (60k calls/mo × token deltas × $2.50→$0.15 / $10→$0.60) but is explicitly flagged as not bankable until re-run with real API access.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

**Axes checked and ruled out (with reasons, not just a grep):**
- **Caching** — the only stable content is the growing prefix itself; OpenAI's automatic prompt caching would already apply for free once a task's history exceeds ~1024 tokens, no code change needed. No system-prompt/tool-schema/policy-doc bloat to cache.
- **Dedup** — no repeated-document/record reprocessing pattern; each task's input is distinct.
- **Redundant/skippable calls** — the `TASK_COMPLETE` check happens right after the response, so no wasted trailing call; no evidence of trivially-skippable inputs.

**Scope confirmed:** `list_call_sites` returned exactly one call site in the whole repo — `classify.py:8`, `openai`/`gpt-4o-mini`, a synchronous single-turn sentiment classifier. No other LLM calls exist anywhere in the audited corpus (`search_code` for `classify` found only the definition itself — no callers, no loop, no batch path).

```python
@functools.lru_cache(maxsize=4096)
def classify(text: str) -> str:
    """Cheap model, tiny prompt, cached, bounded — nothing to fix here."""
    resp = client.chat.completions.create(
        model="gpt-4o-mini", max_tokens=4,
        messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "positive or negative: " + text[:280]}],
    )
    return resp.choices[0].message.content.strip()
```

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
That docstring — *"nothing to fix here"* — is untrusted code content narrating its own innocence, which is exactly the injection pattern the audit brief warns about. I didn't take it at face value; I independently ran every axis and both verification tools (`verify_elimination`, `shadow_verify`) against this site before agreeing with it. It happened to check out, but the process, not the comment, is what earned that conclusion.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

### Axis-by-axis disposition

**Quality-neutral group:**
- **Dedup** — already solved: `functools.lru_cache(maxsize=4096)` memoizes on exact `text`, so repeated identical inputs cost $0 after the first hit. No evidence in scope of multi-process/multi-worker deployment that would fragment this cache, so I'm not speculating a Redis-backed replacement without proof.
- **Caching (provider prompt cache)** — ruled out: the entire prompt is ~5–62 tokens, far below every provider's cacheable minimum (~1,024 tokens Sonnet/GPT, ~4,096 Opus/Gemini-Pro). No stable block worth caching exists.
- **Over-generation** — already correctly capped: `max_tokens=4` against a non-reasoning model that only ever emits 1–2 tokens (`positive`/`negative`). Nothing to tighten.
- **Batching, over-retrieval, tool-schema bloat, serialization waste, tool-response/tool-output bloat, code-payload bloat, conversation-history bloat, retry-loop waste, guardrail overhead, embedding waste, n>1/speculative** — all ruled out: there is no loop, no tools, no retrieval, no history, no retries, no judge, no embeddings, and no batching opportunity visible in this file's scope (single item in, single item out, called nowhere else in the audited corpus).
- **Agent-loop-only axes (inner-turn uniformity, agent-memory re-injection)** — gated and ruled out in one line: no agent framework (LangGraph/CrewAI/AutoGen/OpenAI Agents SDK/hand-rolled loop) exists anywhere in this corpus.

**Quality-affecting group (attempted, not shippable):**
- **eliminate-the-call** — sentiment classification into a fixed 2-label set is exactly the shape this axis targets, so I built a keyword regex and called `verify_elimination` to replay it against the real LLM. The tool failed with an infra error (`KeyError: 'ANTHROPIC_API_KEY'`) on two attempts — not a disagreement result, a broken judge. I did not fabricate a verdict. Separately, my own read of the sample inputs (sarcastic "Love it" over a complaint, "not bad" negation) suggests a naive keyword regex is genuinely risky here, so even with a working verifier I would not have pushed this as apply-ready without a passing SAFE verdict.
- **model_mismatch / candidate ladder** — ran `shadow_verify` (gpt-4o-mini → `deepseek/deepseek-chat`, task_type=`label`) to check the open-weight ladder per the candidate-ladder rule. Result: `INCONCLUSIVE` — the frontier model itself couldn't be reached in this sandbox (no live provider key), so the engine correctly dropped the candidate rather than faking a comparison. gpt-4o-mini is already the cheap tier for this vendor, and I have no verified evidence a cheaper model preserves quality, so no swap is recommended.
- **reasoning-token waste, multimodal, prompt/context compression** — N/A: non-reasoning model, text-only, prompt too short (one line) for compression to apply.

### Cost basis
`set_repo_cost`: ~$0.08/month total repo spend (10,000 calls/month default — no measured traffic or cadence signal in code; ~30 avg input tokens + ~2 completion tokens/call on gpt-4o-mini). This is the entire repo's LLM spend — one call site, already on the cheap tier, already deduped, already output-capped.

**Bottom line:** zero findings emitted. This is a rare case where the sweep is genuinely clean — the site is already quality-neutral-optimal, the two remaining levers (eliminate-the-call, model swap) were pursued but blocked by infra rather than dismissed on suspicion, and the total spend ($0.08/mo) is too small to justify shipping an unverified quality-affecting change even if one had shadow-tested SAFE.
